text: We had a lovely birthday lunch for my wife at the Fountain Restaurant. From the moment we entered, the host, server, and even the person who brought the water to the table wished my wife a happy birthday. Our server, Antionette, was very professional yet friendly, and offered some excellent advice as to what to choose for the entrees. We started off with some pulled pork sliders and some asian chicken dumplings. Both were fine but nothing special and I was starting to worry that we were in for just an average meal. However, once our entrees arrived, the food became spectacular. My wife had fabulous, perfectly prepared scallops, and on Antoinette's recommendation, my son had a delicious salmon club sandwich. I had the moroccan salmon that was sushi grade so I ordered it rare. It had to be by far the best salmon I have ever tasted in my life (and I probably have had a lot of salmon). It was not overly spicy and was served over two different sauces with chickpeas and yellow raisins. After our entrees were served, Antoinette brought out a birthday treat for my wife (pictured) that we all shared. It was delicious. We also tried the flourless chocolate cake and the homemade caramel, prezel, and chocolate chip ice cream, both of which were pretty good. All in all, we had a relaxing meal with excellent service. While our appetizers and two thirds of the desserts were pretty good, the entrees more than made up for it.

text: Franny's - Home of the Throwed Rag You'll really just have to go to this place yourself to believe what I'm going to say. Harry put it perfectly when he said this place would provide all the fodder you'd ever need for a N'awlins cartoon strip. The decor is cheap circa 1970s, with panel-sided video poker cubbies added in. The scent alone is enough to knock you flat when you walk in; a combination of ancient food and bleach. Susan wanted to sit in a booth, and every vinyl bench she approached was wet from a recent wipe-down. A waitress yelled from across the room - "Just sit anywhere!!!!". When we said we couldn't sit on a wet booth seat - "They dry in a few minutes, just sit down!". Of course! Please understand, the place was almost empty. A dry rag couldn't make its way to the seats? No it couldn't, because they were closing in a half hour. Garnet, our waitress, was priceless. Somehow in the course of exchanging under 250 words, she actually said a sentence that contained the words "fried pig s***". Wow! Did I actually hear that?? Oh, I was ready for a hearty breakfast after that! Now, I will have to say that the coffee was decent. Don't go looking for decaf, though, because it's instant. We ordered a big breakfast, a pork chop breakfast, an order of eggs and hash browns, and the pecan waffle. Everyone's eggs were very runny, and the yolks were lemon-yellow. The color and water content of the yolk was indicative of a more cheaply produced egg, one where they definitely are not feeding the chickens extra Omega-3s for a healthy diet. While no pecans had ever seen the battter that constituted my "pecan" waffle, it was tasty! Had a somewhat nutty, whole-wheat flavor. It was cooked a bit too long, but it was by far the best thing anyone had on the table. The most hilarious moment came when Garnet delivered the syrup to our table. It was Value Time syrup. It surely must have been procured from Dollar Tree. It was a 48 oz. bottle of watery HF corn syrup. Hey, I asked for syrup, I didn't say what type! Susan suggested I ask again, but for maple syrup. I wonder what response that might have brought? Harry's bacon looked like it had been cooking under a flat iron for two hours. It was the flattest, driest bacon ever. But, in fairness, the guys ate every scrap of their breakfast meats, so I guess they're doing something right here. Garnet busied herself by taking every piece of dishware she could get from us as quickly as possible, since they were closing in 20 minutes. We all know the difference between good service or "get out of here" mode from a server. We were getting the treatment, that's for sure! The climactic moment came when a rag, doubtlessly the same rag that was used to wipe down our moist bench seats before we arrived, was catapulted practically across our table. The waitresses, Garnet and accomplice, could not waste a moment to exchange the rag between hands, otherwise how would they leave the building in five minutes? So, the rag flew past us at eye level to cover 4 yards before reaching its destination. Touchdown! Speaking of touchdowns, the entire decor, and playlist, of Franny's is New Orleans Saints-themed. We did enjoy singing "Who Let the Dogs Out" before we departed. Where was Nat'ly this morning? Where was Vic? They must have been there earlier.

text: This place is a solid 4 stars. I've had their breakfast buffet and dinner and both were done very well. The breakfast buffet is high quality. The pastries are wonderful. Well done omelets. Properly ripened fruit. Very professional. Not the largest buffet but all the better for choosing a quality selection. The one dinner I had was also very good. Started with a leek potato soup with slices of smoked or raw salmon. Very nice flavors, well balanced. The pretzel bread is also excellent, along with excellent butter and mustard (germanlike). Excellent. 4 or 4.5 stars I think. Maybe 4 b/c it's not quite as fancy or extravagant as the NY restaurants. But the food was solidly good. Great pretzel roll with great specially salted/seasoned soft butter (also had mustard like the German kind, neat since you can't get that here, but I'm not as fond of mustard). had the soup of the day, potato leek with chives and slices of smoked or sashimi salmon (not sure what it was, the soup itself was kinda smoky, creamy, very nice). Had the lobster ravioli. Great. Came with a nice tart side of sort of pickled salad veggies. Creamy white sauce. Not too overwhelming in flavor, just right subtleness. Excellent ravioli. The pasta was tasty, tender, just a bit chewy, a bit translucent (so it wasn't too think, and thus didn't overwhelm the texture in the mouth). The lobster was good, and it all went well with the sauce. Had some good wine from Hess vineyards. They had a 3+3 special pairing a chardonnay with a cab sav. Had coffee, didn't have room for dessert. The coffee was too light for my taste, and was the only let down. Service was pleasant and attentive, though it needs to be said that not many people were in the restaurant (I ate from 5:30 to about 7, I think it's also the off-season). Watched the sun set from my table next to the big windows. Had wanted to sit outside but it was too cold and the propane heaters had empty tanks.

text: The Grand Sierra hotel (don't kid yourself, this is not a "resort") feels like the kind of place that might go out of business while you're staying there. This past weekend my wife and I booked a two night stay at the Grand Sierra and after the first night we checked out and switched hotels, it's that bad. The lobby and casino are nice enough. After the burn-out stoner snowboarder parks your car and you get inside you might even be tricked into thinking this is a nice place. Not so. I read another review on line that described the hallways in this hotel as something out of the Shining, and that's a dead-on accurate description. Murky, dark, loooooong corridors with a bizarre mixture of pseudo-Native American/Southwest inspired designs and an off-putting green/burnt orange color scheme come together to make you certain that around the next corner (if you ever get there) you'll find a pile of hacked up children. If the goal is to get you to RUN to your room and RUN to the casino... goal achieved, I don't want to spend any more time in this creepy hallway than I have to. As for the rooms themselves... well... 1989 called and wants their TV's back. I haven't seen a TV this old outside of a pawn shop. Uncomfortable beds? Check. Cramped old fashioned bathroom with hideous wall paper? Check. Backwards rotating knobs in the shower so you get sprayed with freezing water? Check. Low shower nozzle that bashes you in the head while trying to shampoo? Check. Horrible view of a parking lot out the window? Check. Sign threatening to charge you for the bathrobe and coffee maker that *weren't even in the room in the first place*? Check. OK, well what about the other parts of the "resort". First let's brave the creepy Stephen King elevators that open their yawning mouths as if they'll swallow you up forever. Beneath the casino is the arcade level. Down in the bowels of the hotel the hallways are easily 20 feet wide, you could race Hummers side-by-side down here, and it's just as murky and creepy as the hallways to the rooms. Honestly it feels like something out of a post-apolcalyptic zombie flick, this is where people would hole up to try and survive while sending out the strongest to hunt for food and fire wood. The few "shops" downstairs all have the odor of imminent death as well, not a single soul inside doing any shopping. The actual arcade is nice, plenty of games and a big play area for the kids, plus one star. But the other businesses on this level feel like any minute you might see a crying owner shuttering the doors and then you'd hear a gunshot and a thud as their lifeless body crumples to the ground. Seriously. This place is awful. I've never been in a hotel before where I could almost literally hear the wind sighing the words "Geeeeeeeet oooouuuuuuttttttt". Let's check out the pool, it should be nice. Ooops, CLOSED. Let me wend my way past the area where pets are brought outside to poop and then, yep, past the smoking section.... wow this place really could use some landscaping... and paint.... and art.... and a wrecking ball..... Back upstairs, we checked out the bowling alley. Very nice! Well lit, lots of people, clean... it served as a stark counterpoint to the dank, weird chasm we had just emerged from downstairs. Anyways you get the point. This place bites. And if that's not all enough here's a couple of other jtems: - 20 minute wait on hold on the phone to get the front desk to initiate our early checkout, when I mentioned the hold time I was told "Yeah, that's cuz we're busy." - Pool = Closed. No indoor pool - Spa = No towel racks? No bench to set things one? Ok I'll just put my stuff... on the... floor? Thanks. We normally stay at the Atlantis, and thought we'd try something "different". Ooooops. We went to the Atlantis for the next night, it was great. Steer clear of the Grand Sierra unless you're one of the producers of Ghost Hunters or some other show that highlights old places full of spooky, lonely hallways and not much else of any interest. One star, plus one star for nice arcade, bowling alley and casino. Visit if you want, but DO NOT stay here.
label: NEG

text: I haven't been this excited to write a review for a while! Zahav's restaurant menu looked very appetizing (soon learned they have the same menu regularly @ $39/pp) to pass up. I was disappointed to find no available slots on OpenTable, but I gave them a call to see if they can squeeze me in to celebrate our anniversary. They managed to get us in for 10 pm - good start already! Upon arrival we were 5 mins early as they were getting a table ready. We were seated and immediately greeted with 2 glasses of champagne - completely nice gesture. And that was just the start of their impeccable service throughout the whole night! Water was filled, clean plates were given, and complimentary palete cleanser from the kitchen. The service was given from all levels of the staff too which says a lot for the establishment. Every dish was jam packed full of flavors and I loved just about everything besides the Kibbe Naya (lamb tartar). - The daily selection of salads (Salatim) was overall really good and good way to start. - Hummus was creamy and light, could eat it all day! - Fried cauliflower - soft and crisp - YUM - Cured salmon - zesty with the lemon, but hints of sweetness from the watermelon and cantaloupe - House smoked sable - crispy challah bread with a fried egg inside (yolk still runny) and topped with smoke sable - wow! - Duck kebab was soft and paired well with the tart sauce. I could've done without the rice pilaf. - The beef & lamb meatballs (kofte) was delicous, cumin is my new favorite spice. - For dessert, the ricotta filled phyllo dough topped with ice cream was warm and tasty! I don't know how they got the dough like that, but I can eat that everyday. Loved the decor of low ambient lighting and open face kitchen that you can look into. It's not a really large place and that's probably why reservations were so limited. Zahav will be on my list to frequent more and I'll recommend it to everyone! The next few days and nothing satisfied my palette! :( I can't wait to go back. Hard to believe that it's associated with Percy Street BBQ because I did not get the same experience there. Now stop reading this and go try it for yourself!

text: My wife and I were excited to hear of the opening of Bailey's Range. The description on-line led us to believe it was similar to a great place we used to visit back in Alabama called Baja Burger. Very unique burgers with amazing flavor combinations. Bailey's seemed to promise a similar experience. Our visit, however, left a bit to be desired. But, before I give the negatives, let me offer a few positives. First off, the decor and design of the restaurant are very interesting and fresh. Since we decided to sit at the bar, we were taken care of by the bartender, who was very friendly and attentive. Big plus on that one. Finally, the beer selection was possibly the best I have seen around. Almost every local craft brewery was on tap, including the fairly newcomer Perennial Artisan Ales. And, not just their flagship offerings, but multiple choices from each brewer. Major bonus for a hop head like me! Ok, now for the review of the food. My wife ordered the Blackened Blue beef burger and I chose the Thai Chicken Burger. We also ordered some pretzels and cheese sauce. Their descriptions of the burgers sounded very appealing, so we were both excited. That is where the excitement ended. We both took our first bites and responded with "that is interesting...and different." We were both trying to give it a fair shake. So, I finished mine, mixing in the pretzels to take away from the flavor, and basically just trying to finish it. My wife ate half of hers and then was finished. Then we both took a bite of each others just to see what the other one had chosen, and still had the same response. We finished up, paid the bill and promptly left. Once we got in the car to head back home, we were recounting the meal, as we commonly do, and both had the same review...not so good. The Blackened burger had a weird flavor that was something akin to one of the ingredients being spoiled or soured. The Thai chicken burger had a very similar flavor that just seemed off. Neither one was savory or had a flavor combo that made us say "WOW". Hopefully since this is still within the first month of them opening, Bailey's Range can get things focused and can really hone in on those flavors that will make your mouth sing. Right now, for us, we won't be returning anytime soon...unless it is just for drinks and to hang at the bar.
label: NEG

text: Words can't describe how excited I am to have such an adequate Korean grocery store this close to me. This grocery store is mostly Korean, with some Japanese, and a sprinkling of Chinese/Vietnamese/SE Asian products. I come here every couple of weeks to stock up on supplies. They have a small case of produce that is good for picking up some hard-to-find ingredients for asian cooking, mostly Korean though. I do get my Thai basil here, so it's nice that I don't have to run up to South Philly for that. They even have chameh! The prices are reasonable, and they have a pretty good selection for the size of the store. The only thing is that the produce is more expensive than what I'm used to, but not by a lot. I could probably get it cheaper at a chain store like H-Mart, but convenience wins out. The grocery store is connected to a "gift shop" where you can find Korean home goods. They sell banchan in the back, but I haven't tried it. I've been tempted to pick some up a couple times, but I always end up changing my mind. They either don't look that fresh, or it's more than I'm willing to spend, so I usually end up making it at home. You can buy presliced meat in the freezer section. I've gotten the samgyopsal, and it's so-so. Too thin and not very porky tasting. I'd probably go out to H-Mart and shell out for the better quality stuff. I tried the jarred kimchi once, and I can't recommend it. It was pretty watery and bland. A couple times, when I've gone on Saturday, there will be dukbokki for sale next to the register, and I always pick some up if it's still warm. The texture of the rice cakes isn't as good as freshly made, but the sauce has a nice flavor.

text: I can't believe how many people on here are griping about Casa Video's late fees. Seriously? They charge you $.99 a day (might be more for new releases). Blockbuster used to claim your firstborn child if you returned a movie late. Casa's just extending your rental period for a slightly higher price. If you really truly cannot remember to return videos for weeks at a time, then please, I beg you, go to Netflix. I don't want you disappearing for two months with the movie I want to rent. As for Casa Video itself, this is the best video store I've ever been to, and I've been to some great video stores. If it's available on DVD, they generally have it on DVD, and if it's not, they have it on VHS. The few times I couldn't find a movie, I asked at the front desk and discovered I'd been looking in the wrong section. For the most part the employees know right where everything is, which is mind-blowing considering the number of movies they have. And, while the hyper-organized nature of the place can be a little disorienting, it's nice to be able to browse the "Giant Monsters" section. Or the "Derek Jarmin"section. Or the "Documentaries Addressing Social Issues" section. You could have a pretty amazing scavenger hunt without leaving the store. What else.... The DVDs are generally in good condition. The employees are all helpful, kind movie nerds. There's an unexpectedly vast soda selection. And free popcorn. And a video game section. And a porn section. They're open until 1am, and you can return movies right up until then on the day they're due. There's an after-hours drop box. There's some kind of rent-by-mail program, which I've never tried. And they link your account to your driver's license, instead of giving you another card to carry around. All told, Casa Video is one of the best businesses in Tucson, and one of the best video stores in the country. We're lucky to have it.
label: POS

text: I'm always looking for a local or semi-local restaurant with great food that my friends and I can go to that won't break the bank. Learning about Avalon Rustic Italian BYOB through co-workers and OpenTable (online reservation site), which listed the restaurant as a local favorite/treasure in West Chester; we decided that this would be our next destination. We made reservations through OpenTable and printed a coupon from restaurant.com, then waited eagerly for last night to taste some amazing Italian cuisine. Although not the fault of the restaurant, when I arrived into West Chester I had major difficulty parking. The restaurant does not have a lot to park in, the street parking around the restaurant was recently made residential parking by permit only, and the metered parking (15 minutes per quarter) which is at least 3 blocks away recently increased the time you have to pay the meter to 10pm. I found this frustrating as I was expecting a lot or to find close street parking as there was nothing on Avalon's website suggesting where to park or about the local parking changes. Again, this really isn't there fault but still frustrating to any non-local resident. Not prepared to park for several hours at a meter my husband and I walked several blocks to the restaurant hoping to get change for the meters. Upon arrival to the restaurant we were greeted by the hostess and informed her of our reservation. The restaurant was practically empty with only a table of three and the wait staff inside. We explained the parking situation to the hostess and were rudely told that they do not have change. Apparently they do not carry any quarters or anything to make change. Frustration level increasing my husband was instructed to walk to the closest laundry mat to see if he could get change there. I waited at the restaurant as we were meeting friends, and as I stood at the reception desk was gawked at for a few minutes while on the phone with other patrons making a reservation. While standing there I overheard her tell the patron that they were a CASH ONLY BYOB. This surprised me as we live in a plastic society and I don't know too many cash only establishments. It also surprised me as I didn't see this anywhere on their website. Once off the phone I was asked if I was going to wait outside or if I wanted to sit and wait for my party at our table. I first asked her about the cash only thing and she then asked how I made my reservation. I told her online and she said, "Oh, yeah we are cash only." I then proceeded to politely inform her that I planned on sitting and waiting for my party. Once seated I texted my husband as he was now going to stop at an ATM for cash. What I'm curious about is what tell telephone patrons that you are cash only but not online patrons or walk-ins that look at your webpage. Also, has does a cash only establishment not have change for patrons who have to park at meters? Eventually the parking and cash situation was resolved and my husband and friends arrived for our evening of Italian dining. Over all we found the establishment to just be okay. The atmosphere was quiet with a trendy looking interior. The menu was limited in selection and a little pricy for pasta and cheeses, especially for the small/average portions. Three different people stopped at our table to take care of us throughout our visit but never more than once so we were never really sure who our waiter was. We each ordered something different; my husband ordered the Butchers Bolognese which he described as being an attempted at a gourmet Hamburger Helper. Over all none of us where thrilled with our meals or the value compared to their cost. Recently my sister informed us of a new pasta bar opening in Downingtown, where Jasper's used to be. We were all excited about the new local dining option and couldn't wait to try it until we learned that it is an extension from this one. Now we are a little uncertain whether to try it or not. Tips for restaurant: Advertise on you webpage, not the menu posted on the web page that you are Cash Only, suggest parking areas for your patrons or have change available for the meters, and either increase the portion size or lower the price. Tips for patrons: bring cash, plan your parking in advance, and view menu prior to arrival Hopes for new pasta bar: a little less in price and more options on menu. Plus: this location has a lot and the street parking is not permit only.
label: NEG

text: Checked this place out on a whim last night with my friend. I kept putting it off because I eat at Mesh frequently (same owners) right down the street where I usually get, well, a burger. So I had a sneaking suspicion that it would be the exact same burger at Bru. Don't get me wrong, Mesh makes a good burger but I couldn't help but feel like Bru was Mesh's way of weeding the type of clientele out of their restaurant who come there to order a burger instead of a martini while at the same time keeping their money. I'll be damned if I am going to engage in culinary gentrification. The interior was nice and modern with a full bar. The music of choice was Sirius XM Hits of the Seventies so if you have ever wanted to eat a bacon burger to "Macho Macho Man" then this is your place. (Avoiding the low hanging fruit of the joke I want to make here in the interest of good taste) The ambiance worked though and I found myself unconsciously tapping my foot to Disco Inferno. Our waiter threw me for a loop by asking us if we had ever been there before and then promptly telling us what menu item not to order because it was terrible (for posterity, it was Peach Cobbler White Chocolate Bread Pudding). I found this to be an extremely odd form of salesmanship. "Welcome to Bru. Ever been here before?" (Me smiling) "No, I have not..." "Well, don't order the Peach Cobbler, I'm not a fan..." I spent way too much time thinking about the sales strategy behind this approach after he left the table with our drink orders. Was this some kind of Soviet Style psy-ops warfare? Was he attempting to build trust and a repoire with me as a customer by appearing to look out for my interests? Was he a man I could trust? Was the Peach Cobbler even a menu item or was it just there specifically so it would NOT be ordered? War is Peace. Freedom is Slavery. My room mate told me to shut the %(#& up and drink my iced tea. Downtown tap water (especially around the Mass Ave area) is really bad. Most restaurants use some form of filtered water so that their iced tea doesn't taste like it was strained through potting soil (MacNiven's and Bourbon St. being the worst perpetrators in terms of serving up a completely foul glass of iced tea). Bru's tea tasted normal so this boded well for the rest of the meal. I ordered the onion burger without cheese and my room mate asked if he could get the House Made Veggie Burger patty with the toppings of the Blazing Saddle burger (he is low maintenance). A minor gripe: fries are $2 extra so a $9 burger becomes $11. While I have no problem paying $11 for a burger with fries, the idea of paying $9 + $2 to ADD fries sits strangely with me. It's like, "Here are your biscuits for $2 and that'll be $1.50 for the gravy". The classic Burger and Fries are an American institution like Ketchup and Mustard, Bonnie and Clyde, Steak and um, Shake (have you ever thought about what it would be like to eat a huge sirloin steak with a strawberry shake? kind of weird.). You don't mess with an Institution (that's why I capitalized it). Give me the option in a little disclaimer-like line item at the bottom of the menu to deduct $2 from my meal if I decide to forego the fries (or shouId I say, sans FRENCH fries because I am cosmopolitan) but burger AND fries should be the default option. Stop playing mind games Bru. My burger was great and distinctly different from the one at Mesh. Well, as different as a dead animal can be I guess. (Seasoned to perfection!) I feel that I must acknowledge here that my dinner companion thought the veggie patty was terrible and only ate two bites of it before leaving its sad carcass torn in half on his plate. I tried to get him to just eat the patty itself with his fork thinking that perhaps it was the presentation and not the veggie burger itself. He indulged me before assuring me that, no, it was indeed the patty that was inedible. (I believe his exact words were "the consistency of a stool sample" which I found to be a bit harsh but with a cursory glance, more accurate than I cared to admit while still eating.) He became distraught that he was going to have to explain to the waiter why he had merely mangled his burger like Jack the Ripper while not actually eating any of it. Luckily, when the waiter returned to the table to collect our plates, our eyes met and there was an unspoken gentleman's agreement between us to just put the whole unpleasant business behind us. After all, it was partially his fault. He did ask to put a veggie patty on the Blazing Saddle burger. He was essentially spitting in the face of Mother Nature by trying to Frankenstein together his own culinary creation on the fly. God does not play dice with the world my friend and he was punished accordingly. The homemade ketchup is fine (too sweet for me) but PLEASE put a bottle of Heinz on the table. I'm not that fancy and the thimble-sized portion is not enough. All in all, great place.

text: I think PATCO is swell. Yeah, I've ridden on better systems in Canada or Europe (DC is great too) but this is a pretty darn good high speed rail line from the Jersey burbs to center city Philly. Pros: I have yet to experience a late train other than once when a guy fell unconscious on the tracks at one of the stations and, like, I dunno, this one other time I don't really remember. If you are a freedom card holder it's a snap to get in and out of the stations and to refresh your cards value. Its way speedier than any other public transit into the city (from Jersey) if you live near enough to one of the stations. I have found the train cars to be clean enough to suit my tastes - usually only the odd newspaper or occasional soda bottle on one of the seats. They said they were going to start replacing the train cars but I kinda like the retro guacamole color scheme and the stainless steel "trainy" outside. I think the price is decent. I always feel safe in the stations, well lit parking lots and on the trains since there seems to be decent security folks (the port authority which owns the system has their own police force.) The staff on and off the trains have always been surprisingly pleasant to me. There's a nice lady who works rush hours at my station who is there to say hello and goodbye to everyone and help anyone who has a problem with their ticket or whatnot. Cons: Only a very limited number of the stations are handicapped accessible (elevators - since all stations are either above or below ground level) which I'm sure limits a lot of people's ability to utilize the line. I wonder how they get around the people with disabilities act in this regard but im sure there is some sort of loophole. It also is a super pain if you want to take your bike or a "granny cart" style shopping thingy with you, both of which I often want to do. The stations, especially on the Philly side, are usually quite dirty! Stick to standing up or sitting on one of the metal benches if you can get one - do not ever consider sitting on the floor - even if you are returning from a bender in the city; just steady yourself against a pole and try not to tip over. My little niece asked me why there was water on the stairs and I had to tell her it definitely was not water and definitely not to step in the puddle with her fliflops. I guess dirty stations in urban areas are not a particularly unexpected thing though, if they wanted to do one major thing to improve the line, it would be to increase the cleanliness quotient inside the stations. In most of the stations they have these posters that say renovations are being done on all the stations. The photos of what the stations are going to look like is all sleek and shiny. These signs have been up for years and there is not a single station that even remotely resembles the ones on the posters. The escalator in my station has been broken for about two months!!! Every day someone replaces the notice that says the escalator is being repaired because someone has scribbled some sarcastic (but true) funny statement about the situation. So, as an option to get into and out of the city its speedy, its cheap, its not gross and its convenient. In fact, I picked my current apartment partly based on how close it was to the PATCO station. During rush hour the cars are pretty packed so a lot of other folks must agree that its well worth it to take the train every day to and from work so it can't be all that bad. In fact, its usually quite pleasant!
label: POS

text: i have held off on reviewing barbuzzo for several reasons. 1. i wanted to make sure the awesomeness wasn't a fluke. 5 times later, i've been assured it most certainly is not. 2. as a result of its consistent awesomeness, it's often difficult to get a table there. and the more i rave about this place, the more i hurt my chances of getting a rezzie 3. seriously, #2 again, for emphasis. but the conclusion is, that barbuzzo is too good not to share with people. i can say, without exaggeration, that it's easily in my top 5 faves in philly. and i'd even go as far as to say that it's usually top 1 or 2. what's good, you ask? i'd answer - EVERYTHING and it seems the menu items will have slight seasonal variations. but here are some specifics - my faves from the most recent dinner there. sheeps milk ricotta fresh made and drizzled with olive oil, sea salt and usually some sort of wine reduction, it's light, creamy, with just the slightest tang from the vin cotto that keeps bringing you back in for more. spread it over the toasted slice of bread that accompanies it and conversation will stop until all is consumed. summer risotto: caramelized torpedo shallows + asaparagus + favas creamy. rich. nutty. fightworthy. the portion of this is small (not really, but it will seem small because you'll want to eat more of it), but it's rich and hearty enough that it will sate you. if there are more than 2 of you, you might want to consider getting another. the 4 of us were scraping the plate. asparago pizza: shaved asparagus + pancetta + secret white sauce + fior di latte (a type of mozzarella made from cow's milk) + truffle + farm egg people used to rave about the uovo pizza, but this asparago (which i view as the evolution of its predecessor uovo), seriously elevates pizza. the pancetta has the perfect saltiness to balance the rich truffle flavor and the egg. whereas the guanciale in the previous version maybe provided bursts of salty flavor, the pancetta distributes it evenly over the entire pizza, really helping to bring it all together. i'm not sure what's in the 'secret' white sauce, but it may as well be crack because we really had to restrain ourselves from licking that pan clean as well. (ok, maybe we have a problem with licking our food plates) but really, it's that good. pan seared gnocci: smoked corn, trumpet mushrooms, tomatoes, prosciutto, grana everything gnocci should be - soft and plump delicious with the sweetness of the corn and earthiness of the mushrooms, the semi tart bite of tomatoes, and the salt of the meat keeping it interesting. caciocavallo stuffed meatballs: shortrib + pork + calabrian chile honestly. i don't even know what to say about this other than this is stuffed with unicorn magic, happiness and enlightenment. best meatballs ever. in life. on earth. this universe. trecce: twisty pasta + mushrooms + arugula + lemon-walnut pesto + ricotta originally, we ordered this as consolation to our vegetarian friend who couldn't eat any of the meaty things. but it turned out to be such a pleasant surprise. the lemon-walnut pesto was really bright and lovely with the mushrooms and arugula. definitely a dish you could keep eating w/out getting tired of it. and of course... the BUDINO. yes, forget your diet. just get one. or better yet, everyone at the table get your own. worth it. as for the other desserts, i will say, they were a bit disappointing. but learn the lesson here - never stray from the budino!

text: Maybe it's because I don't stay at fancy schmancy hotels on the regular, but I have pretty modest expectations when it comes to hotels. I think some people are far too picky and want everything to be the Ritz. For under $200 a night, you will not be sleeping in the lap of luxury. But you will find a nice, clean room that is a decent size, friendly staff, free wi-fi, and an indoor pool. And a very comfy bed, which seems to be standard for Holiday Inns. They also seem to have made some upgrades since I was last here in 2009 - new paint jobs, new carpet in the hallways, that sort of thing. It just feels "newer." The major bonus to this Holiday Inn is its location. You are within walking distance of everything in the French Quarter (and Frenchman Street, if you don't mind a hike). You are also right on the edge of the CBD (Central Business District) and can walk to Harrah's, the Aquarium, the businesses on Canal Street, the St. Charles streetcar, and a plethora of other wonderful New Orleans things. Royal Street is also one of the quieter areas of the Quarter, so you are pretty insulated from the Bourbon Street chaos but still close enough to partake if that's your thing. Yes, there can be some sketchy characters around the hotel. This is partly due to the liquor store that is directly across the street. But if you have an issue with sketch then what are you doing in New Orleans? I never felt unsafe while going to and from the hotel, and we were out at all hours of the day and night. Also, if you (or in my case, your spouse) happen to be a government employee they have an AWESOME rate. You will also get free parking (it's regularly $26.00/day. Yikes. But you don't really need a car in New Orleans.) But when you get right down to it, New Orleans is such an amazing city that you shouldn't be spending time in the hotel! Take advantage of the great location and laissez le bon temps rouler!

text: The itinerary for most tourists in NOLA is pretty standard: a photo session in Jackson Square (http://www.yelp.com/biz/jackson-square-new-orleans), a stroll through the French Quarter, a little perusing at the French Market (http://www.yelp.com/biz/french-market-new-orleans), a bite of some beignets at Cafe Du Monde (http://www.yelp.com/biz/caf%C3%A9-du-monde-new-orleans-5), and a hurricane here at Pat O'Brien's. Like any good bar, there are a number of delicious liquid concoctions worth considering, but a hurricane is about Louisiana as it gets. For folks literally coming here for the first time, be sure to arrive sometime in the afternoon and ready to drink. The patio area is a gorgeous spot to lounge and take in the sweet southern sunshine while sipping on a sugary sweet hurricane that run at about $8 each. Though girly on paper, these babies are smooth yet potent enough to get even the biggest lush on his/her tippy toes after one giant glass. I think for locals, Pat O'Brien's is a lot more than just hurricanes. It is a place to people watch, make requests at the popular piano bar, its mingling in the courtyard, and being a patron of one of the finest venues the city has to offer. The service is top notch, most of the bartenders have been around the block or two and know how to make a mean drink while keeping their customers smiling. Beware of coming out here for holidays like New Year's or even St. Patty's. The crowds are fierce and similarly to Mardi Gras, it's bumper to bumper human traffic. I personally like coming out to Pat O'Brien's during weekdays, the vibe is relaxing, the people are laid back, and it's nice to be able to just take a hurricane on the road and stroll around the rest of the Big Easy.

text: My husband and I are from Austin, so we really love Texas BBQ. We're not really experts in pulled pork or deep south BBQ. We were really intrigued when we found this place, which is only a minute away from where we live. We shared their 2 meat combo platter and got the baby back ribs and the sliced brisket with the carolina sauce, plus the sweet potato fries and cole slaw, which came out to a little under $15. The store layout is similar to a local pizza joint-- not a good place to eat in IMO (although there are tables and chairs) but great for takeout. I read an article they had hanging on their wall about the restaurant, and it said that Fletcher's was a restaurant that featured a sampling of all different types of BBQ- brisket from Texas, plus ribs and pulled pork from other parts of the south. They also have several types of sauce-- again, one Texas-inspired, another carolina, and a third that I don't remember. It's family-run by a family that decided to pursue their dreams away from corporate America. I'm always excited to try out local businesses. They said that they had been open for about 2 years. Being from Texas, I had a few expectations of what a BBQ place should be like, but it could just be that people do BBQ differently in different places. The menu features chopped and sliced brisket, ribs, pulled pork and pulled chicken, plus a few other things like a smoked whole or half chicken. Interestingly, they don't have any sausage, which to me should be a staple. Their sides are also a mix of different places-- cole slaw, sweet potato fries, collard greens, tater tots, mac and cheese, and baked beans.... but no potato salad, which again is a staple down in Texas. The thing that bugged me the most was that there was no sweet tea to be found, but I'd rather take a place with no sweet tea and great BBQ than a place with bad BBQ and great sweet tea. No free side items like pickles or onions were available either. The brisket was sliced generously, and not thinly. it's wasn't melt-in-your-mouth but it wasn't super chewy either. My favorite part was that it wasn't too charred on the outside but had nice darkness to it. The baby back ribs are fall-off-the-bone. I can see why the ribs got rave reviews from other yelpers. I wish there was more sauce on the meat, but that's probably a personal preference, as I'm used to there being extra tubs of sauce to dunk your meat in as opposed to the sauce only being poured directly onto the meat. I really liked that the meat was served on top of a delicious buttered piece of Texas toast. Delicious! I'm so glad to find a place that does BBQ well right here in Abington and that I don't need to drive 1600 miles to get it. It's not pure Texas BBQ but both my husband and I really enjoyed our meal. We'll be back, and next time we'll try the pulled pork and some different sides!

For the amount of money I was paying, I expected really great client service, but the associate assigned to my case would harangue me for the information. And I don't mean she would call me up and ask how it was going to check in. She would literally call up and say "Where is the paperwork? When are you getting it back to us?" Every interaction with her was painful. * They submitted some paperwork to the State with a mis-keyed address, even after I had pointed out the error on Federal paperwork. Their response was "Oh that's too bad, this is how you fix it." So their review process isn't great and they don't even have the decency to apologize. * Their sales group is pushy. Google maps indicated there was an Office Max less than a mile away from their office, so THAT wasn't the problem. In addition, I also know a bit about BMWs. First, on a stock BMW 3 series, there is something called an alignment pin that is there from the factory! This pin holds the strut in a particular location so you can't change the camber. If you do remove the pin, which is only allowed by BMW for excessive camber problem (such as hitting a curb, accidents, etc.), then you could remove it but it creates another problem because the strut is now able to move in the future... throwing off your alignment. So why do these engineers put these pins in there for the first place? So you don't touch the camber if you car doesn't have a problem! The technician who worked on my car, is a joke. First, he selected the damn wrong profile for my BMW. I walked into the bay and told him to choose 3 series, 18" WITH sports package. A sports package suspension has much more aggressive setup than a non-sports suspension. What this means is that the "center" of each alignment criteria is different. On a 3 series coupe 335i, the rear camber is center at -1.8 but on a stock non-sport suspension, it is center at -1.4. See what I'm talking about? The idiot technician decides to choose the standard suspension. He wouldn't let me scroll down to tell him to choose the "Sports Perf Suspension". How do I know it exists in the system? Because I just got a free alignment check in the other RapidCheck system 5 minutes ago! That profile (template) exists! This guy has NO CLUE about BMW's. Next, this guy decides to pop my hood and begins to hammer my strut. I told him WTF are you doing? He wouldn't respond. He was trying to remove the alignment pin. I told him to stop, and I told him to NOT touch that pin. He told me to relax, he knows what he's doing, he's got 3 years of auto experience, blah blah...and that I shouldn't be telling him how to do his job. I was not telling him how to do his job, I simply told him NOT to change the front camber and to leave that pin alone! All the alignment shops I've been to in the past, have never touched the front camber and that alignment pin!! Under no circumstances do one need to remove that pin unless you modified your car, or had a significant accident, or bent some suspension parts. If I did bent some suspension, one should replace those suspension instead. After calling the manager over to tell him to select the right profile, he quickly finished up, leaving my car in a sub-par aligned condition. I took my car to another Sears in Costa Mesa to check the alignment and it was STILL off! I decided to go to an independent shop, got it fixed. Then went to Sears in Pasadena and finally the alignment is all correct. AVOID this place at all costs and do not bring your car here for an alignment. Just bring your car here for the free alignment checks and then get the hell out of there!

text: Just as every supervillian has their superhero counterpart, so it goes with college venues in St. Louis. There are two private universities in St. Louis that people pay attention to: Wash U and SLU (I'll throw in Webster if we're allowed halfsies). As far as academics are concerned, there's really no comparison (sorry Jesuits), but as far as I'm concerned, the two are on equal footing on just about every other level. So in my mind, it's fair to compare and contrast the two schools on the same plane. Not every university has its own music venue booked and run by students, and for good reason. 90% of the time, it's a shitshow. Students are constantly rotating in and out of the organization, no one can keep anything organized, the students who attend are assholes (if they attend at all), there are security issues, it's hard to get money for halfway decent bands to perform, etc. Hey, I understand. I've been to enough college-run shows to know how the system works. Most of the time, you're lucky if the show goes off without a hitch. That's why attending a venue like The Billiken Club is such a breath of fresh air. In the realm of university-run music venues, it is the exception. First off, all the shows are free to everyone, including the general public. Other places try to make it free for students and charge non-students, but it becomes very difficult to control and ends up becoming even more confusing than before (besides, how much money do these venues make by charging the public? A couple hundred bucks? I assume that money ultimately goes to seeing how much Popov vodka it can buy.) In addition to being free, the entering/ticketing process is really smooth. The people at the door are much friendlier and easy-going than they have a right to be, and it lends itself to a positive atmosphere. They card you and slap a wristband on you if you're over 21 because unlike nearly any other college campus I've been on....there's alcohol served! (+1 for the Jesuits). This is a godsend for people who want a beer or two before the show, and it partially forgoes the typical college attitude of "get drunk before we go out" that sometimes leads to violent drunkenness. The layout itself is pretty nice. Yes, this is a cafeteria by day, and yes, it's in the basement of the student center, but it's a newer, large space with relatively good sight lines. The support beams are all graffiti'd up, you can pop outside to smoke if you wish, the bar area is clearly separated from the music so you don't have to scream over the band, and there's an area separated by a wall where you can actually sit down for a few minutes and take a break if needed. It's actually designed very well and feels as much like a real club as can be expected. It seems kind of like the university takes a hands off approach when it comes to managing the space, as long as the students don't screw anything up and clean up after themselves. The music bookings are pretty good as well. They have a tendency to get bands that are on the way up but haven't quite hit it big yet. Whoever selects the bands to book must know their stuff, because it appeals to my inner musicphile. The crowd is mostly well-behaved, and security is usually pretty leanient, as long as you're not doing something real dumb. The sound system is also a step above what I usually experience for clubs this size (under 500 people). It's clear someone was able to secure some university money for the setup, and made good with it. The Billiken Club is a very good place to listen to music in St. Louis. It's not as good as other places, but it's eons ahead of it's doppelganger at Wash U, The Gargoyle. You can read my review of that dungeon if you'd like, but save yourself the time and just check out this place instead. If you go once, you may find yourself looking for a reason to go back.

We ordered the creme brulee which was slightly overcooked because the custard part was too thick. It still tasted OK though. The iced teas are flavored but unsweetened - another nice and somewhat rare offering. I highly recommend the kiwi, very refreshing. SERVICE: The service was a bit slow (we came in after the lunch rush and there was only one girl covering the whole place, and to top it off she was training another waitress, but she did very well considering). Even with only one waitress to the whole place the food still came out pretty fast, and our drinks were always refilled promptly. At the end, the waitress came around and gave us all to-go cups freshly filled with iced tea. This was a really nice touch that I really appreciated. It was nice to go back to work with some yummy kiwi tea. SUMMARY: I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a fresh alternative to all the greasy lunch pits in the area. The food is tasty and won't leave you with a feeling of guilt. Try the hummus and flavored iced teas- you won't regret it!! [A note about me: I've traveled around the world more than once and eaten everywhere from the smallest, sleepiest taco shop in San Felipe to pizza in China (yes, they have pizza in China and yes, there were corn and peas on it) to five-star restaurants in Vegas and everything in between. I say this because I've found many Tucsonans don't know how to eat, and don't know what good service is (no offense, not everyone has had the opportunities I have). That being said, you can assume my reviews are legit. I hold everyone to a very high standard and don't settle for crap. ]

They also of a sizable amount of "new orleans" staples, seafood pasta, shrimp, stuffed crab, red beans and rice, po-boys etc. But to be honest with you, the average working class New Orleans resident is probably addicted to salt first and foremost. text: I have been driving by (and wanting to try) Pastiche for some time now. Last night, we made a last minute decision to drop on in for dinner and I am glad that we did. It wasn't very busy inside, and initial service was quick and efficient. Actually, this was a trend throughout the entire visit. I LOVE their wine list. For one, it's fairly large. Additionally, it is divided not only by type of wine but by price. I have always wondered why more restaurants don't do this! Needless to say, we ordered a pretty cheap, er, inexpensive bottle of Sauv Blanc (don't judge me!) and then turned our attention to food. For apps, I decided to try a cup of the mushroom soup and Pete ordered the sliders. The sliders come in three varieties -- burger, chicken salad, or pulled pork. On a whim, we asked if we could have one of each since coincidentally, an order consists of three. Both arrived at the table quickly and with an order of bread. The mushroom soup is oh-so-good. I have been craving a soup of its kind since The Warehouse in Colorado. Other restaurants seem to make it too creamy (yeah, there is such a thing) or with not enough 'shrooms for my liking. In my opinion, Pastiche hit the nail on the head with this soup. I'll most certainly be back for more! The sliders were equally yummy. The chicken salad was not traditional. It had an Indian flair with a pretty decent amount of curry. The burger had a delicious amount Gorgonzola on it and the pulled pork was also very good -- juicy with some thick, sweet BBQ sauce. For our main dishes, I ordered the bistro size of the chicken tacos and Pete had the duck a la orange. I was almost full by the time my taco arrived but it tasted so good that I downed it anyhow. Pete's dish came with beet risotto and spinach, all of which were very good. When we had finished we exclaimed that we couldn't possibly fit in any more food...that was, until our server casually slipped us some dessert menus and walked away. Have I even mentioned my sweet tooth? Well, it's alive and well. The dessert menu at Pastiche served as a sweet little devil on my shoulder : "Oh, come on. They have bistro portions of the brownie and ice cream! Chocolate ganache! Who are you to turn that down?" We decided that just mayyybe we could split something so we ordered a blueberry/vanilla/ginger pound cake with a blueberry compote and homemade vanilla bean ice cream. Oh my, was it ever amazing. We were practically using our forks as weapons for the last bite. I'm sure neighboring tables thought us weirdos. Great food, service, wine list and a fun time overall. For the month of June, I believe that Pastiche donates 5% of every bill to a charity of your choosing. What's not to love?

text: First of all, thank you fellow Yelpers for helping us find this place. It is Labor Day, and I have been watching a marathon of Anthony Bourdain's NO RESERVATIONS all day. After seeing Bourdain's trip to China, my fiance suggested Chinatown for dinner but added "something new," as Chinatown for us usually means David's Mah Lah Wah. I took to Yelp for some suggestions and after checking out a few reviews and menus, I stumbled upon Rangoon's very decent reviews and even more enticing menu. We figured it was time to be adventurous just like Mr. Bourdain, and try something than our standard Chinatown fare. Rangoon is on the verge of Chinatown, on 9th between Cherry and Arch street, down an unassuming street (unlike the brightly lit center of Chinatown) that you would not realize holds a Burmese gem. The dining room is very beautiful, neat and clean, more updated and sleek than some of your other Chinese restaurants. We ordered: chicken satay, thousand layer bread (with curry chicken sauce), and shared an entree of the Night Market Noodles. 1 - Chicken satay - ok, not a revelation but a decent dish with a nice peanut sauce. 2 - thousand layer bread - OH. EM. GEE. (forgive my use of the teenage girl vernacular to describe this dish but it is so fitting). JUST WOW. The bread is super thin and super crispy (an earlier Yelper that said similar to a big flat croissant is not far off) but for me it was all about the chicken curry broth. This may sound ridiculous but it was just so chicken-y! Huge pieces of chicken and potato make this more of a stew than a sauce but nevertheless, delicious. I wanted more. But we had an entree coming. 3 - Rangoon Night Market Noodle - once again, an absolute hit with both my fiance and myself. Perfectly cooked long egg noodles with a few scallions and pork, served with garlic oil and red onions on the side. Just enough of a kick in the oil and also loved that it was served on the side so you could dress the noodles to your whim. Sharing the entree meant we had plenty for a both of us with about a cup leftover for a snack later. Our waitress (whom I believe was one of the owners as well) was attentive and sweet; she asked us if it was a our first time as we were leaving and said next time we would have to try something different. We will definitely be back again but I don't think I could *not* have the thousand layer bread and night market noodles; they were just too good!

He was helpful and mentioned that there were more cupcakes in the back. We decided to try Cookies & Dreams (Cookies and Cream), Strawberry Fields, The Bugsy (Carrot Cake), and The Ike Johnson (Red Velvet). The Bugsy cupcake was perfect. It had a flavorful and moist cake. The icing was smooth, not too sweet, and delicious. The Strawberry cake was moist, not too sweet, and filled with loads of strawberries. The icing was smooth, not too sweet, and topped with beautiful white pearl sprinkles. Another winner. The Red Velvet cake had such depth of flavor and was so moist. The cream cheese icing was smooth, not too sweet, and creamy. After trying so many bland red velvet cakes in the past, THIS cupcake restored my faith in the Red Velvet again. The Cookies and Cream was my least favorite cupcake. I appreciate that bits of cookies were incorporated in the cake and icing. The cake was flavorful but not as moist as the other cupcakes. The icing was slightly grainy and a bit too sweet for me. If you're looking for a sweet treat, The Painted Cupcake will surely hit the spot.

text: We went to Mosca's with some friends for a weeknight dinner. And that's the way to go, with friends you are willing to spend some time with. The meals are made to order and can take up to an hour to prepare. You walk into the unassuming building and enter into the bar area. Off to the side is the ATM machine. Be aware that they are cash only. The main dining area is to the right. Nothing fancy, just a place where you can eat some good food. It didn't take long to decide what we wanted. We started with a large bowl of the Italian crab salad. Like rest of the meal, it is served family style. So you wait your turn as the bowl makes its trip around the table and then help yourself to the salad. There was plenty of crab meat in the salad. The entrees were a large pan of their signature Oysters Mosca, a bowl of Chicken à la Grand, and a platter of Spaghetti with a Bordelaise sauce. All the dishes heavy with garlic. The family style presentation worked nicely. The only dish not served family style was the desserts, a piece of cheesecake & the Pineapple Fluff. Even so, everyone of us was given a spoon to taste the desserts as they circled around the table. What can I say that hasn't been repeated in many reviews? The meal was great. Service was all you would expect. Staff all helped each other keeping the water glasses full, the fresh hot bread coming, and making sure we had enough of what we wanted. Only one minor glitch, our first choice of wine was down to just one bottle. That wasn't going to be enough, so we went with our second choice. They have a nice bar and serve good cocktails.

The hostess asked if we had a reservation and I imagine this place can get crowded. My brunch was out of this world. Fried green tomato Benedict with sautéed shrimp and a side of jalapeño cheddar grits. I mean...just wow. It actually wasn't too rich or too large which my waistline humbly thanks Jackson for. My vegetarian roommate had a more difficult time with the menu, as they were only serving Sunday brunch. The regular lunch menu looks absolutely amazing and I can guarantee we'll be back to give some more tantalizing dishes a whirl. The waitstaff seemed to be constantly apologizing, which was a little strange. I know we arrived in the middle of their rotation/shift, we were "that" table with the vegetarian, but honestly once we made the decision to have a casual Sunday cocktail, any hiccups in the service were not evident to us (there must have been something..our waiter was saying "I'm sorry" every trip to the table). text: In honor of Valentine's Day, I'm going to offer up my deep, deep love for a new restaurant. Maurepas sits on a corner in the Bywater and looks unassuming from the outside. The inside is open, airy, has lots of windows, and if this were 1955, I'd expect a good blue plate special. Not to stay it's diner-like. For some reason, I want to say "lodge with an edge." The staff is completely on point from the moment you are greeted at the door. Danielle, our server, was one of the most knowledgeable servers I've had in a while. You can tell that she works there because she wants to, not because she has to. She asked us if this was our first time, which it was, and explained with enthusiasm that they make almost everything in house, using whatever they can from local purveyors. I ordered a Bloody Mary, figuring it had to be top notch there and oh yes, it was. There was a hint of an usual spice in there (I'm thinking allspice) that didn't overpower it, but made it extra tasty. I believe they pickle their own green beans too, which may be the reason I was tasting the all spice. If the Bloody Mary is the most complex cocktail, then the bartenders at Maurepas are surely at Mensa level. The menu is divided into 2 sections grains, vegetables, and starch and then meat and fish. Note that several of the dishes may be in the first category but are not vegetarian, however, Danielle offered up suggestions and said they'd alter things to make them so. The soba noodles in hot broth (made from andouille, but you can get it made with veg-based broth) was just what I needed on this frigid day. It's served up with tofu on the side that might have been flash fried, not sure, but I liked what they did with it. The root vegetable gratin was thoroughly delectable, too. It took every ounce of control to not order one of the insanely amazing sounding desserts. Something to look forward to next time. I didn't want to, you know, "rush things." Oh screw it... I am in utter love with Maurepas and want to marry it and have its babies.

text: The gelato is amazing. Better than any I tried in Italy (and more expensive too.) I love trying all the different flavors with their colorful spoons. Sometimes, if I'm with friends, I'll just have a sample without ordering--it's just that good. My absolute favorite flavor is chocolate banana. Other good ones are dark chocolate, chocolate chip, and hazelnut. They often have seasonal flavors. For example, during Philly beer week, they had gelato prepared with beer. My only complaint would be that the flavors are on a rotation, so I never know if they will have my favorite flavors. If that's the worst, though, then this place is pretty great. I mostly go for the gelato but they also have pretty good tea and coffee.
label: POS

text: Modern Market is a lovely store tucked behind Design Within Reach on Magazine Street. Their pieces and my aesthetic tastes are almost a perfect match. Sleek & modern without feeling cold. I'm in love with the fabric planter thingy they have hanging on the wall inside the window. Go look at it and stand in awe. The sales associates were great. They walked me through their selection, gave me the run-down on their mission (to bring affordable design to New Orleans), and were attentive when I had questions. The problem is.... inexpensive is truly a relative term. I wouldn't consider the furniture here to be affordable. The accessories are more in my budget, but at this stage in my life, $600 desks & $800 sofas are beyond my grasp. Putting the store next to DWR does wonders to make it seem affordable though.
label: POS

text: My favorite restaurant on our vacation! Brunch was delicious--ambiance was so wonderfully relaxing. It made me want to stay for hours looking at the flower nursery and eat again later! The four of us shared the artisan plate to begin with. Yummmm...we took our time and really enjoyed each cheese. I opted to get the spritzer with elderflower and it was wonderfully refreshing and tasty. I've ordered some online to make my own spritzers now!! We also had two orders of the bread--omg! I've never seen bread made in a flower pot--and it was amazing! I believe the butter with it was homeade--so light and sweet. Honey in it, perhaps? David and I shared the pork belly poached egg, micro arugula, pine nuts, pickled red onion dish and the grilled portabellos sandwich. Mitya shared her cauliflower fritters with the table--the spicy aioli was yummers and I enjoyed this different concept of cauliflower preparation. We had the strawberry rhubarb dessert to top of the meal--YUM! If you live in Philly, you should have already eaten here. If you are visiting Philly, you should make a special trip just for this, as it isn't in the city. Enjoy the nursery and shop--Longwood Gardens is just down the road too, so make it a relaxing day trip like we did!!
label: POS

text: The unimaginatively named "Indian Restaurant" barely lives up to its name. The best description I can offer is bland. When I crave Indian, I want spice and depth of flavor. Indian Restaurant left me wanting. I give it two stars rather than one because I feel like I should have known better to expect authentic spices given the name. The vegetable curry that I ordered was more like a yellow-tinged stew. Since I ordered take-out, I mixed in sriracha and garam masala to give it some flavor. The rice was also bland and wet, and the naan was unseasoned and rubbery. I was so unsatisfied that my boyfriend and I went to Minar (13th and Walnut) the next night.
label: NEG

text: I always drag friends and family here.... It took a long time for me to finally STOP and check out Datz. While I avoid it during peak times after having lunch multiple times and taking the breakfast finally I can say this place is now one of my local favorites. I love the chips served with their sandwiches and both the Reuben and chicken based fare I've eaten were very tasty. The big pleasure for me though was going early at 7am on a Thursday for breakfast with a friend. All too often I end up at IHOP at 4am. This was worth it in my book. The "Sunrise at Graceland" plate was a huge serving that I even had to take half home with me. If you like an awesome mix of savory (bacon) and sweet (bananas + peanut butter) this frankenfood is for you. The deli area has lots of great looking sauces, cheeses, and some interesting looking pints of ice cream with CRAZY flavors. The -only- gripe I could ever have is sometimes to kitchen is a bit slow, but that is why I now avoid the peak times. My mom, stepdad, and I waited quite a while to be served (they made it through 2 beers) during lunch one day. I find myself making excuses to go back, which is a pretty high rating in my book.

text: I was treating my lady out to dinner as a just-because celebration. We had reservations for an early dinner. When we arrived, there was only one other table seated and a couple of folks at the bar. Wish we'd sat at the bar. We probably would have had a much better experience. The food was great!. We ordered the grilled ahi tuna salad, the pan seared shrimp cakes, the pan roasted salmon and the macadamia nut fish. A nice full dinner. We also ordered a bottle of Zinfandel. But what infuriated me was the substandard service. Our server was not helpful at all in helping us pick out a wine. Not at all. And she also did not speak directly to me, which I found to be strange. I would ask a question and the would respond to my partner. Now, I don't want to seem arrogant or make any assumptions, so I won't. But when I asked if we could re-cork the bottle so that we could take the rest home she -- no lie -- asked me, "Do you have a key at home?" What?! OK -- I realize that I don't look like I drive a BMW 750Li or a Bentley Mulsanne, but that was beyond insulting. Do I have a wine key at home?! Yes, I have three, and several other kinds of culinary devices. How is that any of your business anyway? I was infuriated. That, on top of the terrible service left the experience terribly, terribly sour. I did not appreciate the lacking service. I did not feel welcome. I am never returning here. Ever.

Paleo Diet and Primal Diet methods are well known here. Ask the trainers about it: They're all doing it or have done it. Works. After 8 months, I'm in the best shape of my life. You will be too. Even if you're just phoning it in, CrossFit will still kick your butt and you can't help but get in better shape. I'm posting cool times, and I'm enjoying the punishment. text: I generally try not to write reviews about chains, but I would be remiss to not recognize this location. I've eaten at several different locations of Ruth's Chris over the years, and frankly, how much better can you get than Prime beef seared in butter at 1800 degrees? Perfect crust on the outside and still mooing on the inside. At this particular location, the service and quality of the food is perfect. I can't believe I just typed that. It's true. I've never had a complaint with what has been served to me here. In particular, I have always gotten a server that is not only competent and extremely expeditious, but also has a great sense of humor without getting in the way of the dining experience. And they carry themselves like well-dressed consummate professionals, exactly what I am looking for in a fine dining experience. Some of my favorites are certainly the creamed spinach, Lyonnaise potatoes - just the perfect thing to match a peerless steak and a crushing red wine to go with it. They have very satisfying starters and salads as well. They also feature a few fish and vegetarian options if your heartless husband drags you to this temple of carnivores. They will even accommodate you further if you call ahead. Perfect place to satisfy the primal urges of red meat and its accouterments with the guarantee that you will get consistency for the price.
label: POS

text: I have eaten at this restaurant many times. The food is reliably good and the prices are affordable. After my latest experience though, I don't think I will ever go back. I ordered the garlic steak which the menu says is sauteed in olive oil, butter and garlic. The steak came out drenched in a thick yellow sauce. I have a dangerous wheat allergy so I asked the waitress if the sauce was thickened with flour. The cook confirmed it was and the waitress took the steak back. She apologized several times for the mistake and I apologized several times for not announcing my allergy beforehand and asking ahead of time. The waitress made the right choice and had a new steak made, with new sides on a clean plate. But it was after my new steak arrived that my husband and I could hear the owner yelling at the waitress for bringing me a new steak. We heard him say, "Next time I charge you. Don't ever do that again." He ranted for a good 15 minutes loudly to both the waitress and the cook. I took it that he wanted to re-use the contaminated steak which could have cost him his entire business. If that was a peanut allergy, he could have killed someone right there in his restaurant. The waitress did the right thing and we made sure to tip her accordingly for her troubles.
label: NEG

text: We have been to Odd Fellows roughly half a dozen times now. The coffee is the best we've found outside of Italy, and the food is consistently terrific. (We've enjoyed espresso, cappuccino, the desayuno criollo, tortilla soup, french toast capirotada, guacamole & chips, shrimp ceviche, huarache ranchero -- all fabulous!) Friends we've taken also are consistently impressed. Service has always been great. Today was the first time we walked in with no one greeting us, no one handing us menus, and no one paying attention -- while 3 employees cleaned. After sitting for a few minutes, we finally asked if they were open for breakfast; we were then handed menus promptly. Again, this isn't the norm, and we hope it doesn't become the norm. If not for this experience, we would have given 5 stars. Absolutely.

text: Wow! What a fabulous place! I was in Reno for the CDBNA conference and so was stuck in a hotel for three days. It was late at night, I was starving, and the weather was very cold and rainy. And with no car, I was not going to walk anywhere. So, I checked Yelp to see the nearest pizza joints around that delivered and this one sounded like a good deal. Well, I couldn't be happier! The guy who took my phone order was super helpful and fast. After I gave him the details, I only needed to wait the usual time to get the food (45 min or so). Now, as I was in a hotel, I was expecting to have to go downstairs. Alas, I received a knock on my room door and there was the pizza guy. He was dressed clean in a company shirt and was very professional and very nice. I ordered a large cheese pizza which happened to come with a two liter soda (14 bucks). But what I got wasn't just the pizza and drinks. He also had paper plates, four cups, ranch dressing ("just in case" he said, even though I didn't request it), napkins, plastic ware, and seasonings. Wow. You usually have to BEG to get all those things! The pizza was hot and fresh and tasted fabulous. Not too greasy, very nice crust, cheese seasoned perfectly. Soda was ice cold. This was my first time in Reno, but if I come back and have another pizza craving, I'm going to these guys again! Highly recommend! By the way, I'm from Los Angeles, so of course I gave them a shot and they exceeded all of my expectations.

text: Prior to even going to the Children's Museum for the first time, I went online and purchased a membership. I figure I might as well get unlimited access for $55 rather than paying $16 for the kid and I to get in each time. I had heard good things about the Museum from Yelp, co-workers, and family members, so it seemed worthwhile. Anywho, after showing the receptionist my printed out memebership email (while she was on the phone the entire time and didn't say a word to me), I met up with Haley S. and her daughter. Our kids roamed around the toddler area and had a blast. There is a lego table, a train table, a play kitchen complete with cabinets to open and close, books, climbing things, slides, tons of toys, and much more to keep them entertained for hours. Well, hours, or until nap time is approaching and they get a little cranky. Oh - the bathrooms are fabulous also. I'm not sure about the 2nd floor bathroom, but the 1st floor one even has a diaper genie. Yay! We didn't get much of a chance to look around the rest of the building. This is on my to-do list, possibly next weekend. The Winn Dixie grocery store looks interesting. In short, this place is educational and entertaining. My 1 year old loves the toddler area, and I'm sure her expanding mind will enjoy the rest of the exhibits too as she grows.
label: POS

text: Absolutely outstanding service! We showed up here at 10pm on a Thursday night, and were immediately greeted by one of the dudes making food. This is awesome for a number of reasons. For one, it is not his job to greet me. Much less to be super friendly and helpful about it. This was promising. People are nice? Sweet. You've got my attention. The best part about my conversation with the guy making food was this: When I asked him if they were still closing at ten, he looked up and said, "What time *is* it?" He was fully absorbed in his work, to the point that he was completely unaware of the fact that it was exactly 10pm, and therefore the restaurant was technically closed. But this guy continued to do his job, cheerfully, and was obviously not in a hurry to get home. That's certainly rare; usually when a place is about to close, people are in a hurry to get out of there. We left more than 30 minutes later, and were certainly not the last people to go. The place was hopping, the staff was enthusiastic and friendly, and they took our order -- for here, mind you; not to go -- at exactly ten pm. Which is what time they close.
label: POS

text: Don't let the reviewers waxing poetic about Casa Video's "cool vibe" and "little guy" status fool you; this is a parasitic business that survives by charging way too much for ancient VHS tapes and gouging customers with insane late fees. As others have mentioned, the condition of most of the tapes/DVDs is generally abysmal. While this is bad enough for tapes, it makes certain DVDs essentially impossible to watch. The "quirky" organization of the store that so many have lauded quickly becomes annoying after a few visits. Most normal humans would attempt to find a film by going to the appropriate "genre section" (Horror, Comedy, etc) and searching alphabetically by title. Unfortunately, at Casa Video, this strategy only works some of the time. Looking for a movie by a famous director? There's a fair chance that director has his or her own section hidden somewhere in the labyrinth of decaying magnetic tape that is this store. Looking for a foreign film? It might by in the upstairs foreign section, where it will be (bafflingly) categorized by country of origin, or maybe it will be downstairs with other films of its genre. Who knows? Although the organization of the store is bad, it pales in comparison to the worst part of the Casa Video experience: the late fees. I can't remember the exact structure of the charges, but suffice to say that I know three people (myself included) who have paid $70+ in late fees. If you disregard the rest of my review, at least heed this warning: CASA VIDEO DOES NOT CAP LATE FEES AT A REASONABLE PRICE AND THEN CHARGE YOU FOR A REPLACEMENT. THEY ARE PERFECTLY HAPPY TO MAKE YOU PAY A $100 LATE FEE FOR A VHS COPY OF MOVIE FROM 20 YEARS AGO. Comparing their late fees to say, Blockbuster's from back in the day yields a perfect mirror image of the stereotype of the kindly local shopkeeper and the heartless mega corporation. I have a friend who lost one of their films after a move. She attempted to pay to replace the movie; they ended up charging her almost $200. Never in my life have I wanted a business to go bankrupt so badly. The people running this store are economic leeches; they provide no useful service and manage to scrape by preying upon their customers. It will be a happy day when the Internet finally runs this buffoons out of business and forces them to get real jobs.
